passage:
In a small town, there is a museum with only one room. It shows old tools, photos, toys, and letters from local families.
Some visitors ask why the town needs such a small museum. The guide answers, "Because small places have history too."
A student named Nina visited for a report. She found a photo of her street from fifty years ago. There were fewer buildings and more fields. She also saw a lunch box like the one her grandfather had described.
Nina realized that history was not only kings, wars, or famous people. It was also ordinary lives before hers.
The tiny museum made the past feel close enough to touch.
